body.heading: Big goals meet real lives
paragraphs: Goals are usually set in a hopeful moment, with an imagined future self who has more time, energy and calm than the real one turns out to have. Then life happens — work swells, family needs grow, health wobbles — and the goal quietly becomes impossible as written.

At that point most people see two options: force it or drop it. There is a third: shrink it. The goal’s direction — fitter, more fluent, more financially calm — can stay exactly the same while its size changes completely.

body.heading: How to shrink well
paragraphs: Cut the target, the timeline or the frequency — one of them, clearly. Read twenty books becomes read ten pages a day. Save a large sum becomes save a small amount every Friday, automatically. Run a race becomes walk most days and run twice a week.

Write the new version down as deliberately as you wrote the old one. A shrunk goal that is written and specific is a plan. A shrunk goal that lives as a vague guilty feeling is just the old goal wearing a disguise.

body.heading: Small and alive beats grand and dead
paragraphs: A modest goal you are actually pursuing teaches you things, builds evidence and keeps the door open to growing it again when life allows. An abandoned grand goal teaches only avoidance.
Shrink without apology, and as often as life requires. The direction is the commitment. The size is just engineering.

takeaway: Keep the direction, cut the size, and let the goal live at a scale your real life can hold.
